endorsements.quote: This will rely on clinician oversight to ‘approve’ the contours and provide feedback to vendors on model performance, 16 with an increased use of multimodal imaging.

Risk assessment and quality assurance of AI technologies to identify sub‐optimal solutions will require RTs to develop and maintain appropriate skills related to model interpretability, explainability and data dependency.

unlisted_practices: Establish a multi-professional team responsible for AI activities, with profession-led implementation.
Engage patients and consumers in the adoption of AI in radiation therapy.
Do not replace all human checks with AI in quality assurance, because model scope and bias can introduce errors.
Document contouring accuracy studies, or at least store them for later analysis.
Prioritize radiation therapist-led research into AI's impact on professional roles, responsibilities and service delivery.
Include AI and machine learning foundations in radiation therapy education curricula through collaboration between academic institutions and clinical departments.
Plan for the professional impact of AI on radiation therapist roles, including burnout, role expansion and redeployment.
Publish evidence-based dose variation thresholds for daily online adaptive radiation therapy before widespread adoption.

screen.reason: Commentary on the role of radiation therapists and considerations for safety, workflow, and oversight when implementing AI in radiation therapy treatment planning.
